To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the development of HT is associated with endothelium dysfunction; (2) the development of hemorrhage is associated with the blood-brain barrier breakdown; (3) the development of both hemorrhagic transformation and blood-brain barrier dysfunction is associated with the increase in the concentration of neuron-specific eno-lase
the development of hemorrhage transformation in the acute phase in ischemic stroke may be associated with endothelial dysfunction and blood-brain barrier injury.
the level of endothelin-1 and neuron-specific enolases in the acute phase in ischemic stroke are associated with hemorrhagic transformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of factors of vascular regulation and endothelial dysfunction in the acute period of ischemic stroke.
the role of markers of endothelium function and blood-brain barrier in the development of hemorrhage in ischemic stroke and the possibility of their use as prognostic factors.
the role of endothelin-1 and its receptors in the regulation of vascular tone and the development of endothelial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of ischemic cerebrovascular disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of HT may be associated with the activation of the renin-angiotensin system, endothelin-1, neuron-specific eno-lase and the increase in sICAM concentration.
the development of HT is associated with endothelium dysfunction and damage to blood-brain barrier.

the markers of endothelium and vascular wall dysfunction, as well as blood-brain barrier injury, may play a predictive and pathogenic role in the development and severity of hemorrhagic transformation of the ischemic stroke lesion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of HT is associated with endothelium damage and the activation of the renin-angiotensin system.
the development of HT is determined not only by blood-brain barrier dysfunction, but also by the regulation of vascular tone.
the development of HT is a multifactorial process, in which endothelial dysfunction and the damage of blood-brain-barrier play an important role.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of endothelium and its markers is of great interest in the study of ischemic stroke.
the use of a combination of markers of endothelial dysfunction and blood-brain barrier in the acute phase may improve the assessment of the risk of HT in patients with ischemia.
the study of the mechanisms of HT development in the acute phase may help to improve the effectiveness of treatment of patients with ischemic strokes.
